children: Holtec is targeting a valuation of up to $10.2 billion in its U.S. initial public offering, the nuclear technology company said on Tuesday, as Wall Street returns from its summer break.
The Camden, New Jersey-based nuclear technology company is seeking up to $900 million by offering 50 million shares priced between $15 and $18 apiece.
The fall stretch is traditionally one of the busiest for new deals, as markets shake off the summer lull and dealmakers rush to bring offerings when investors return after Labor Day.
The listing adds to a string of nuclear IPOs this year as issuers in the sector increasingly pivot to traditional IPOs from blank-check deals.
J.P. Morgan, Guggenheim Securities, Goldman Sachs, Citigroup, and BofA Securities are joint lead book-running managers. Holtec will list on the Nasdaq and Nasdaq Texas under the symbol "HNUC".
